title: Peter Chanel (28 April)
hookLine: a quiet missionary killed on the Pacific island of Futuna, honored as the first martyr of Oceania

lines: A SMALL ISLAND IN THE PACIFIC.
MOST DAYS, HE VISITS AND LISTENS.
THE KING'S SON ASKS FOR BAPTISM.
cards: Not every missionary story has crowds in it.

This one has a small island in the middle of the Pacific, a French priest who has learned the local language, a garden, a hut, and a handful of people interested in what he teaches. Most days, he visits the sick.
He listens. Very little seems to happen. Then the son of the island's king asks to be baptized, and everything changes, fast.

teach.b: Peter Chanel was a French priest who joined the Marists, the Society of Mary, and asked to be sent to the missions. He was sent to Futuna, an island far out in the Pacific.
He learned the language and cared for the sick, and people came to know him for his gentleness.
For a long time, almost nobody asked for baptism. The island's king had welcomed the missionaries at first.
But as a few islanders, and then his own son, began to turn to the new faith, the king came to see it as a threat to his authority.

teach.h: KILLED AFTER THE KING'S SON TURNED.
teach.b: One morning, men sent from the king's side came to Peter's hut and killed him with clubs and an axe. Here the story turns.
Tradition says that soon after his death, the people of Futuna asked for baptism, and the island became Catholic.
The Church honors Peter Chanel as the first martyr of Oceania.

teach.h: IF IT DIE, IT BRINGETH FORTH MUCH FRUIT.
teach.b: Jesus says in the Gospel of John, in the Douay-Rheims: "Unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, itself remaineth alone. But if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit."

That's the shape of Peter's life: a seed that looked wasted. Catholics across the Pacific, from Futuna to New Zealand and Australia, keep his feast. And on Futuna, people keep his memory at the place where he died.

how: Catholics keep Peter Chanel's optional memorial on 28 April; it is kept with special honor in Oceania, and the Marists remember him as one of their own.

games.q: you're Peter, a missionary on a small island. after a long time, almost nobody has asked for baptism. what do you do?
o: give up and ask to be sent home.
keep learning, visiting the sick and listening.
push the king to order baptisms.
games.why: he kept on with small, quiet work. he was killed, and tradition says the island asked for baptism soon after.

practice: Start with one island, Futuna: a garden, a hut, a sick neighbor being visited, or start with the face of someone you know from the Pacific.

Then let the picture widen to Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Papua New Guinea, cities from Auckland to Manila, fishing families, children walking to school, churches singing in island languages, coasts facing rising seas.
If you pray, pray for the peoples of the Pacific; if you don't, let the picture stay wide.
